title: Can synthetic data reproduce real-world findings in epidemiology? A replication study using adversarial random forests
abstract: arXiv:2508.14936v4 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Synthetic data hold substantial potential to address practical challenges in epidemiology due to restricted data access and privacy concerns. However, many current methods suffer from limited quality, high computational demands, and complexity for non-experts. Furthermore, common evaluation strategies for synthetic data often fail to directly reflect statistical utility and measure privacy risks sufficiently. Against this background, a critical underexplored question is whether synthetic data can reliably reproduce key findings from epidemiological research while preserving privacy. We propose adversarial random forests (ARF) as an efficient and convenient method for synthesizing tabular epidemiological data. translated_title: 合成数据能否重现流行病学中的真实世界研究发现？一项基于对抗性随机森林的复制研究
translated_abstract: 由于数据访问受限和隐私问题，合成数据在应对流行病学中的实际挑战方面具有巨大潜力。然而，目前许多方法存在质量有限、计算需求高以及对非专业人员而言过于复杂等问题。此外，常用的合成数据评估策略往往无法直接反映统计效用，也不能充分衡量隐私风险。在此背景下，一个关键且尚未被充分探索的问题是：合成数据能否在保护隐私的同时，可靠地重现流行病学研究的关键发现。我们提出对抗性随机森林（ARF）作为一种高效且便捷的方法，用于合成表格型流行病学数据。为评估其性能，我们复制了六篇流行病学出版物的统计分析，涵盖血压、人体测量、心肌梗死、加速度计测量、孤独感和糖尿病，数据来自德国的
tldr: 该研究提出对抗性随机森林（ARF）作为合成表格型流行病学数据的高效便捷方法，并通过复制六项流行病学研究的统计分析，验证了合成数据能在保护隐私的同时可靠重现真实世界的研究发现。
en_tdlr: This study proposes adversarial random forests (ARF) as an efficient and convenient method for synthesizing tabular epidemiological data, and demonstrates through replicating statistical analyses from six epidemiological publications that synthetic data can reliably reproduce real-world findings while preserving privacy.
